processing: Ripe pu-erh pressed into the bowl-shaped tuo that Xiaguan is known for; as with other shu, the leaf is wet-piled before steaming and pressing.
harvest_season: No specific picking is documented; as with factory ripe tuos, the production year is what is stated.
appearance_dry: A firm, dark brown bowl-shaped tuo with a hollow underside.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as is typical of ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Dark brown fragments and leaf, soft after steeping.
taste_profile: As is typical of ripe factory tuos, an earthy, woody and smooth cup; no detailed notes specific to this tea are well documented.

brewing.notes: Xiaguan tuos are often pressed hard. Pry carefully from the hollow side and rinse once or twice.

vintage_note: As is usual for factory tuos, it would be sold by production year and drunk young or after several years of rest. Little is documented on the specific formats and years of this tea, so read the wrapper closely.
description:
Pu tuo reads as a shortened name for a pu-erh tuo from the Xiaguan factory in Dali, and it is usually taken to mean a ripe one. Little more is documented about it as a separate product, so take this as a description of the type rather than of a defined recipe.

As with other ripe tuos, the leaf is piled and fermented, then steamed and pressed into a small bowl shape. That hollow helps the tuo dry, and a hard pressing makes it slow to break apart.

Expect the familiar shu profile: earth, wood, smoothness and little bitterness. Use very hot water and short early steeps, and let a young tuo air out if the pile smell is strong.

When buying, go by the wrapper rather than the shorthand, since Xiaguan makes several ripe tuos with similar names. Well-known Xiaguan tuos have been counterfeited, so a reliable seller matters.
history: Tuo tea is reported to have been made in Xiaguan from 1902, while the factory itself was set up in 1941 as the Kang-Zang tea factory and renamed Yunnan Xiaguan Tea Factory in the 1950s. Little is documented about this specific product within that history.
